info.title: AmoBot API
info.description:
AmoBot's HTTP API. Every answer is JSON; the panels are static files that render their own pages.

**The panels.** `/api/admin/*` is the owner's panel and `/api/agent/*` an agent's; each has its own session. The
owner signs in with the login kept in config.php and may work in any shop: each request names its shop in the
`X-Shop` header (none means the main shop), and the session itself remembers no shop. An agent signs in with a
one-time link from the main bot and works only in their own bot's shop. Screens both panels have are described once,
under `/api/{panel}/…`; a screen only one panel has is under that panel's prefix. Panel requests send the session
cookie, and a request that changes something also sends `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest` (the CSRF guard).
`/api/app` is public. `/api/install/*` answers only until the shop is installed, and only with the install key in
`X-Install-Key` (the text of storage/install-key.txt, which the first request creates); without it the answer is a
403 on `key`. Every answer carries its request id in `X-Request-Id`; an error answer also has it in its body
(`request_id`), and every log line the request wrote carries the same id.

**The Store API.** `/api/store/v1/{store}/*` is the API of a shop's own website (the main bot's or an agent's). The
store key in the path names the shop. A customer signs in (Telegram, Google, or an email and a password, plus a
second step when two-factor sign-in is on) and gets a bearer token: the `customer` scheme, with no cookie, session or
CSRF header. Pages on the website's origins may call it from a browser: preflight requests are answered, and every
answer, errors included, carries the CORS headers.
- Public: the plans the bot sells now, the status of the servers they are sold on and, while the website shows
  reviews, the approved reviews with their count and average rating. Anyone may then write a review: a guest
  through the website's captcha (only signed-in customers while the website asks for no captcha). A review waits for
  support's approval; sent with a bearer token, it belongs to that customer.
- A signed-in customer manages their account: names, password, two-factor sign-in, the ways they sign in (adding one
  that another account of the shop already has offers a merge, 202) and their signed-in devices. Changing how the
  account signs in (the password, two-factor sign-in, a way in, a merge) also needs a sign-in from the last 15
  minutes, else a 403 whose `WWW-Authenticate` says so; `POST /me/reauthenticate` proves a way in again. A bearer
  token alone cannot change any of it, nor hand a service to another customer (`POST /subscriptions/{id}/transfer`
  asks the same).
- They read their own services (refreshed from the panel, auto-renewal switched, link changed), orders and
  payments, wallet and ledger, referral numbers and notifications. They order through the bot's checkout (a plan, a
  renewal, a wallet top-up, extra traffic, time or devices), each ordering request with an `Idempotency-Key`, and upload a
  card transfer's receipt. They open support tickets, about a service or not, write with or without a picture, close
  them, reopen them by writing, and rate them.
- A form on the site itself (a contact form) may use the website's captcha too: the site's backend asks the shop to
  check the widget's token (`POST /captcha/verify`), so the site never holds the captcha's secret.
- Request bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`). A form is accepted only where a picture may be
  uploaded (a receipt, a ticket message); any other body type is a 415.

**The website's admin API.** `/api/store/v1/{store}/admin/*` gives the shop's admins (customers whose role is admin)
the shop's daily work on its website, with their bearer token. It has the panel operations marked `x-staff`: the
marker's value is the grant the operation needs, or `true` for none.
- It answers only while the website lets admins in (`staff_enabled`).
- While the website asks for a strong sign-in (`staff_strong_sign_in`), a session signed in with a password alone is
  refused: it needs Telegram, Google, or a password with its second step (`POST /me/reauthenticate` can prove one).
- Every operation needs a way in proven on the session within the last 12 hours: an admin's token lasts a working
  day, not the months a customer's does.
- An operation that names a grant works only while the website grants it (`staff_grants`), and it needs a sign-in
  from the last 15 minutes. Approving a payment, which delivers a service, needs one too (`x-staff-recent`).
- Each refusal is a 403 (`StaffRefused`). The shop's configuration (payment methods, the bot's settings, texts and
  keyboards, the report group, the website, who the admins are) is not there at all (404).
- An admin cannot act on themselves: approve or refund their own payment, adjust their own wallet, change their own
  service (days and traffic, switch, move, transfer, delete) or moderate their own review. They cannot touch another admin's or
  an agent's account, approve a payment without a receipt in review, or leave a client on a panel that answers.
  These guards protect only an admin's own account: two admins can do for each other what each is refused for
  themselves, so give the role only to people you trust.
The admin paths are the panel paths, described once: tests/Support/ApiDescription expands each marked operation to
its `/admin` path (the store key instead of the panel, the `customer` bearer scheme, the 401 and the 403).

**Versioning.** The Store API's version is in its address: this is v1. Within v1 an answer only gains fields; no
field is removed, renamed or given another type, and a request keeps accepting what it accepted, so a website keeps
working across the shop's upgrades. A breaking change comes as v2, beside v1. Every refusal and failure uses the one
error shape; its `message` is written for the reader (the customer on the Store API, the admin on the panels).

**The contract.** Both sides are checked against this file. Every request the PHP tests send and every answer they
get must match it (tests/HttpTestCase); every route must be described here, and nothing else; every POST, PUT and
PATCH describes its body or says it takes none (`x-no-body: true`) (tests/Unit/Http/ApiDescriptionTest); and the
panels' TypeScript types are generated from it (`pnpm api:types` writes resources/panel/src/lib/api-types.ts).
Objects are closed: a field the server sends, or a request carries, that is not described here fails the tests.

get.summary: Health check for uptime monitors. Says whether the app and its database answer.
The shop's name and whether it is installed. The panels ask this first.
The installation's progress. Available only until the shop is installed.

post.summary: Save the database settings. They are written to config.php only after the driver's probe connects. A blank secret means empty here, since nothing is stored yet.
Create the shop's tables. Creates the tables missing from the database the previous step saved.
Set the panel's login.
Set the shop's name and address, and the bot's token when one is given.
Finish the installation.
Sign the owner in. The session works in the shop named by `X-Shop`; if that shop does not exist, even the right credentials get a 404.
Start recovering a lost login. Writes a one-time key into the host's files, where only someone with access to them can read it. Asking again while the key is still valid returns the same key.

200.description: Where the key is, and until when it is valid

post.summary: Set a new panel login with the recovery key. This browser is signed in with it, in the shop the request names, and every other session ends. A wrong key counts as a failed sign-in.

200.description: Set; this browser is signed in with the new login

post.summary: Sign an agent in with the code from their one-time link. The main bot gives the link; the session works in the agent's own shop. If another agent is signed in in this browser, the request needs `replace: true`; without it the answer is a 409 on `replace` and the link stays unused, so the panel can ask first.

get.summary: Who is signed in to this panel, and which shop the request works in. For the owner, the shop the request names; for an agent, their own bot's.

post.summary: Sign out of this panel. A session of the other panel in the same browser stays signed in.
Sign the agent out of every other browser. This browser stays signed in. If this session was itself ended meanwhile from another browser, the answer is a 401.

put.summary: Change the panel's login. Every other session ends; this one stays signed in.

get.summary: The shops the owner can open. The main bot's shop first, then each agent's.

The agent's traffic ledger. Newest line first.
The change feed's version of each area. The panel reloads what an area shows when its number moves.

post.summary: Report a panel error to the server log. For errors in the panel's own code, such as a page that failed to render or an unhandled error.

get.summary: The counts of what waits for support. The sidebar shows them beside payments, orders, support tickets and reviews.
The dashboard. The period's figures, compared with the period before.
The system's health. The version, PHP, the bot of the shop the request names and the main bot, and the scheduler. Owner only.

post.summary: Set the webhook of every bot. Each webhook is under APP_URL, which must be HTTPS (else a 422 and no bot is changed). Same as `bot:webhook:set`: a bot that fails does not stop the others.

delete.summary: Delete the webhook of every bot. The bots go back to polling, so `bot:poll` must run. Same as `bot:webhook:delete`.

get.summary: AmoBot's update status. The running version, the newest release (read again from GitHub when the last read is a few hours old), what blocks a self-update, and the current or last update. Owner only.

post.summary: Check GitHub for the newest release now. A 502 when GitHub does not answer; the release read before is kept.

200.description: The update status, with GitHub's answer

post.summary: Start updating to the newest release. A 422 on `version` when it is not the newest release or not newer than the running one; a 409 while an update is already running; a 422 naming what blocks a self-update.

200.description: Started; the run is at its first step

post.summary: Run the update's next step. Does as much of the step as one request has time for: download the release and check its signature, unpack it, check the host, then install it in one request while every other request gets a 503 with `Retry-After`. A refusal is kept on the run (`run.error`). A 409 while another request is working on the update or a scheduled run does not finish in time; a 502 when GitHub does not answer.
Cancel the update before installing starts (`run.cancel`). The downloaded and unpacked files are deleted.

200.description: The update status, with no update running

post.summary: Roll back the last update (`run.rollback`). Puts the replaced version back. Refused once the update changed the database: only a backup can undo that.

Make an order for a customer by hand («افزودن سفارش»), paid and delivered at once.
post.description:
Support makes a new service for the customer: a plan (`plan_id`) on one of its servers that can deliver it now, or
a service of its own numbers (`traffic_gb`, `days`, `devices`; 0 for no limit) on any server that can take one now
(`server_id`). It is named `client_name` when given (held to the rules a buyer's own name is: 3 to 32 Latin
letters, digits, `_` and `-`, taken by the server's panel, free there), else by the shop's pattern. `payment` says
how it is paid: `free` (a gift), `wallet` (`amount` charged to the customer's wallet, while the shop's wallet is
switched on) or `outside` (`amount` support took outside the shop, cash or another card — counted in the
shop's takings). The order is delivered at once, in an agent's shop out of the agent's traffic; the customer is
told once it is, and the report group's «خریدها» says support made it. A delivery that fails leaves the order
`failed` for a retry (`POST /orders/{id}/retry`), which tells the customer.

How each counts: a free order is a gift — no purchase of the customer's (a first-purchase price and a newcomer's
code stay theirs), no takings, no referrer's commission or gift, no cashback, nothing towards loyalty tiers or the
draw. A wallet order is a purchase at that amount (cashback, loyalty and a referral's first-purchase gift count it)
but no takings and no commission: the wallet's money counted when it came in. An outside order is the same
purchase and the shop's takings too, earning the referrer's commission.

A 403 for an admin's own account on the website's admin API. A 422 under the field refused: `status` (an agent's
shop whose selling is suspended: none is made there, by the owner neither, until it sells again), `payment`
(`wallet` while the shop's wallet is switched off), `amount` (not a whole number above zero, or more than the wallet
holds, an agent's credit counting), `plan_id` (not a plan of the shop; in an agent's shop a plan the owner hid, an
unlimited plan, or more traffic than the agent has left), `traffic_gb`, `days`, `devices` (out of bounds; in an
agent's shop 0 traffic, or more than is left), `server_id` (none, one that cannot take it now, or one the owner
keeps from the agent's shop), `client_name`, `note`, and `idempotency_key`.

201.description: Made, paid and delivered — or paid with its delivery failed

200.description: The order the key made before, as it is now

put.summary: Set a customer's groups. Replaces their groups with the ones listed.

200.description: Turned off; the website account as it is now

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: The status tab: an OrderStatus, or `stuck` (paid but not delivered, because the delivery failed or stalled). Empty for all

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: What to sort by. Anything else sorts by creation time

get.summary: One order, as the list shows it.

post.summary: Retry delivering a paid order whose delivery failed or stalled.
Cancel an unpaid order. Its open payments are cancelled with it, including one whose receipt waits for review.

get.summary: All payments. Newest first, or sorted by `sort` and `dir`; with the count of receipts to review and the list's paid total.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: What to sort by. Anything else sorts by creation time

post.summary: Reject receipts waiting for review in bulk: the payments `ids` names, or `all` of them (the oldest 100 a request).
post.description:
Each receipt is rejected as `POST /payments/{id}/reject` rejects one: the payment fails with `note`, its order
stays open (the customer may pay it again until it expires), the customer is told in the bot with the note, and
the receipt's report in the report group loses its buttons. A picture uploaded from the website is deleted too;
one sent in the bot stays with Telegram. The report group's «رسیدها» topic gets one line saying how many and who.
A payment no longer waiting for review is skipped. `all` goes 100 a request, each round sending back the first
answer's `until`: a receipt sent while it runs is left for support. A 422 on `ids` when neither `ids` nor `all` is
sent, both are, or over 100 are named; on `until` that is no date-time; on `note` over 300 characters.

get.summary: One payment, as the list shows it.
The payment's receipt picture. A receipt sent in the bot is fetched from Telegram. A picture the browser can show is sent inline; anything else (a HEIC photo) as a download.

post.summary: Approve a payment and deliver what it paid for. With a receipt in review, or by hand without one.
post.description:
A panel can approve a card transfer with its receipt in review, or by hand without a receipt. An admin on the
website's admin API can approve only a receipt in review, and never their own payment; otherwise the answer is a
403, as it is for a sign-in older than 15 minutes. A payment whose state no longer allows approval is a 422 on
`status`.

post.summary: Reject a receipt.
Cancel an unpaid payment and its open order. If another payment of the order has a receipt waiting for review, only this payment is cancelled and the order stays open for that review.
Remind the customer to pay. The answer says whether the reminder reached them.
Retry the delivery of what a paid payment bought.

Refund a paid payment. For a purchase, a renewal or an agent's traffic, the amount goes to the customer's wallet; a wallet top-up is taken back out of the wallet. What the order gave a service is taken back first: a purchase's service removed (its client off its panel, the service off the shop), a renewal's or an extra's term and traffic taken off the service and its device limit put back (an extra's devices while their period lasts), once; in an agent's shop the traffic it drew goes back to the agent. A 422 on `note` over 190 characters (it becomes the wallet line's description) or on `status`, and also when what the order added is gone or cannot be taken back (a top-up already spent, an agent's traffic already sold, a service whose panel fails, a purchase's service another paid or open order holds, a service handed to another customer since): then nothing is refunded. A service switched off stays off. The service's own refusals (busy, too many panel operations) come as they are.

get.summary: All the shop's services: sold, renewed or given, the free test accounts, and those customers added by their link (`kind` tells them apart). Newest first, or sorted by `sort` and `dir`.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Only the services of this kind. Empty for all

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: What to sort by. Anything else sorts by creation time

get.summary: One service, as the list shows it.

post.summary: Refresh a service's usage and term from its panel.
Add days and traffic to a service, on top of what it has.
Switch a service off on its panel.
Switch a service back on.
Move a service to another server. It keeps its remaining days and traffic.
Delete a service from its panel and from the shop.

get.summary: «انتقال سرویس», before it is done: the shop's customer with this numeric Telegram id who would receive the service, so the form shows them before `POST`. The same refusals as `POST`, nothing changed.

parameters.name: telegram_id
parameters.description: The recipient's numeric Telegram id (Persian digits are read too).

post.summary: Hand a service to another customer of the shop («انتقال سرویس»), found by their numeric Telegram id — support may whatever `transfer_enabled` says. The service keeps its link, term and traffic; its «تمدید خودکار» goes off; both customers are told in the bot — the new one, where its panel can change the link, that the previous one keeps it until they do; a renewal or an extra of it the previous customer left unpaid is cancelled, noted «سرویس این سفارش به حساب دیگری منتقل شد» (one whose receipt waits for review stays, and fails at its delivery), and the previous customer's message names them; the report group's «خریدها» topic hears of it; and its client on the panel takes the new customer's Telegram id and comment, its name unchanged (a panel that fails that is logged, and the transfer stands). A 422 on `status` for a free test account, a service gone from its panel, or one being changed on its panel right then (a delivery under way: try again in a moment); on `telegram_id` for an id that is no number, that names no customer of this shop (they must have started the bot once), the service's own customer, a banned account, or the admin themselves. A 403 for a shop admin's own service.

200.description: Transferred; the service, its new customer on it

get.summary: All support tickets. Latest activity first; searchable by customer, subject or number (`#12` finds that ticket only). Includes the count of open tickets waiting for support.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: The status tab. Empty for all tickets

get.summary: One ticket, with its whole conversation.

post.summary: Answer a ticket as support. Send JSON, or a form to attach a picture. The ticket becomes answered (a closed ticket reopens), the customer is notified (in Telegram with the picture, else by email) and the report group gets the answer. A 422 on `body` (1 to 4000 characters), on `file` (a JPEG, PNG or WebP, at most 10 MB) or on `status` once the ticket has 200 messages. A 503 while the host has less than 200 MB of free disk, or once the shop's uploads for the day reach 1024 MB. A form larger than PHP accepts is a 413; a form field that is not UTF-8 is a 422 on that field.

get.summary: A ticket message's picture. Served from the shop's files or fetched from Telegram. A 404 when the message has no picture or it is gone; a 502 while Telegram cannot be reached.

post.summary: Close a ticket. The customer and the report group are notified. A 422 on `status` when it is already closed.
Reopen a closed ticket. It waits for support again, and its rating is cleared. A 422 on `status` when it is not closed.

get.summary: All reviews written on the website. Newest first; searchable by the signed name, the text, the customer who wrote it or a number (`#12` finds that review only). Includes the count of reviews waiting for support.

parameters.name: status

post.summary: Approve a pending or rejected review. The website shows it from now on (the Store API's `GET /reviews`). A 403 for an admin's own review; a 422 on `status` when it is already approved.
Reject a pending or approved review. It is kept but no longer shown on the website. A 403 for an admin's own review; a 422 on `status` when it is already rejected.

delete.summary: Delete a review, whatever its status. A 403 for an admin's own review.

post.summary: Get a nonce for an id_token sign-in. For Telegram's popup or Google, when signing in, adding a way in or proving one again: the site opens the provider's sign-in with the nonce and sends it back once, with the token. A 429 once this address network asked for 120 nonces, states and codes in 10 minutes (one address can be many customers on a mobile network). A 503 while the shop already holds its maximum of open sign-ins (5000 nonces, each valid for half an hour).

Start a Telegram sign-in by redirect. Returns the address to send the browser to. The site makes the PKCE verifier, keeps it in this browser and sends only its challenge; the shop makes the state (which keeps the challenge) and the nonce. Only `POST /auth/telegram` accepts this state back, together with the verifier (a signed-in customer uses `POST /me/telegram/authorize` instead). A 422 while the website has no client secret, or on `redirect_uri` or `code_challenge`; a 429 once this address network asked for 120 nonces, states and codes in 10 minutes; a 503 while the shop holds its maximum of open sign-ins.

Sign in with Telegram. Send the popup's id_token, or the redirect's code with the state from `POST /auth/telegram/authorize` and the verifier of its challenge. A signed-in customer's state, or a code and state brought back to another browser, signs nobody in. Signs in the shop's customer with that Telegram account, or registers a new customer as the bot does. A 401 when the proof does not hold; a 403 when banned; a 422 when Telegram sign-in is off or a field is missing; a 429 after too many failures from this address network (30 in 15 minutes); a 502 when Telegram cannot be reached.

200.description: Signed in; the bearer token is shown only this once

post.summary: Sign in with Google. Send the id_token Google Identity Services gave the page, with the nonce it was requested with. Signs in the customer with that Google account; else the customer with the email address Google vouches for (that account can sign in with Google from then on, and the customer is notified); else registers a new customer. Google vouches for an address only when `email_verified` is true and it is an @gmail.com or Google Workspace (`hd`) address; any other address is ignored. A 401 when the proof does not hold; a 403 when banned; a 409 when the address belongs to an account that cannot be linked this way (two-factor sign-in is on, or another Google account is linked): the customer signs in their usual way and adds Google from their account. A 422 when Google sign-in is off; a 429 after too many failures from this address network; a 502 when Google cannot be reached.

200.description: Signed in; the bearer token is shown only this once

post.summary: Sign up with an email. Emails a six-digit code to the address (finish with `POST /auth/register/verify`); if the address already has an account, the email says so instead. The answer is the same either way. Asking again sends a new code that replaces the last one. A 422 when email sign-up is off or a field (the captcha included) is invalid. A 429 when a code went to the address in the last minute, the address got its 10 emails today (counted across all shops), this address network sent its 20 an hour or asked too often, or the address is locked after failed codes (10 wrong an hour, 20 a day). A 502 when the email could not be sent. A 503 when the shop sends no email, the shop's or the installation's email budget is spent (60 an hour and 300 a day per shop), or the captcha could not be checked.

202.description: Emailed: a code, or a notice that the address already has an account

post.summary: Finish signing up with the emailed code. Creates the account and signs it in; the referrer, if any, is notified. A 409 when the address got an account meanwhile; a 422 when the code is wrong, expired, used or tried five times (or email sign-up is off); a 429 after too many failures, or when the address's budget of wrong codes is spent (10 an hour, 20 a day, each counted before it is checked).

200.description: Signed up and signed in; the bearer token is shown only this once

post.summary: Sign in with an email and password. If the account has two-factor sign-in on, the answer is a 202 with a challenge instead (finish with `POST /auth/login/2fa`). A 401 for a wrong email or password (one answer for both, so it never reveals which addresses have an account); a 403 when banned; a 422 on an invalid field (the captcha included); a 429 after too many failures from this address network (30 in 15 minutes) or on this account (50, from all addresses); a 503 when the captcha could not be checked.

200.description: Signed in; the bearer token is shown only this once

202.description: The password is right; the account needs its authenticator app's code. No session yet

post.summary: Finish a password sign-in with its second step. Send the challenge with the six-digit code from the account's authenticator app (Persian digits accepted; each code works once) or one of its recovery codes (used up). If the challenge came from a password reset, the new password is set now and every other session of the account ends. A 401 when the challenge is no longer valid (expired, five wrong codes, or two-factor turned off since): sign in again. A 403 when banned; a 422 when a field is missing or the code is wrong. A 429 after too many failures from this address network or on this account, or when the account's second-step budget is spent: 10 codes an hour and 20 a day, counted before each is checked, whoever tries them (the customer is notified once a day).

200.description: Signed in; the bearer token is shown only this once

post.summary: Start a password reset. Emails a six-digit code when the address has an account; an address without one gets an email saying so, at most once a day (a second request that day sends nothing). The answer is the same either way. A 422 on the address or the captcha. A 429 when a code went to the address in the last minute, the address got its 10 emails today (counted across all shops), this address network sent its 20 an hour or asked too often, or the address is locked after failed codes (10 wrong an hour, 20 a day). A 502 when the email could not be sent. A 503 when the shop sends no email, the shop's or the installation's email budget is spent, or the captcha could not be checked.

202.description: Accepted; a code is on its way if the address has an account

post.summary: Set a new password with the code from `POST /auth/password/forgot`. The password is saved, every session of the account ends, this device is signed in and the customer is notified. If two-factor sign-in is on (a reset does not turn it off), the answer is a 202 with a challenge and nothing changes yet: `POST /auth/login/2fa` sets the new password. A 403 when banned; a 422 on an invalid field, or a code that is wrong, expired, used or tried five times; a 429 after too many failures, or when the address's budget of wrong codes is spent (10 an hour, 20 a day, each counted before it is checked; the account is notified once a day).

200.description: Set and signed in; the bearer token is shown only this once

202.description: The code is right; the account needs its authenticator app's code, which sets the new password and signs in. Nothing changed yet

get.summary: Get a challenge for the captcha widget. For a widget that fetches its challenge from the shop: ALTCHA's `challengeurl`. A new challenge every time, never cached; it is solved and sent once, within 15 minutes. `action` binds it to a form, so its solution passes no form of another action. A 404 while the website asks for no captcha, or for one whose widget makes its own challenge (Turnstile); a 422 on `action`.

post.summary: Check a captcha token for the site's own backend. For the site's own forms (a contact form): the shop holds the captcha's secret and says whether the token passed for the action the backend names, where it was solved (Turnstile reports the host, which must be the website's address or one of its origins) and why it failed. Call it server to server: a browser's claim that it passed proves nothing. Each token is accepted once (an ALTCHA solution, for the 15 minutes its challenge lives). A 200 whether or not it passed; a 409 while the website asks for no captcha; a 422 on `token`, `action` or `remoteip`. A 429 past the website's 3000 checks in 10 minutes (the backend is one address for all its visitors), or past 120 refused tokens in that time from the visitor's network: the one `remoteip` names, else the backend's own. So pass the visitor's address, and a bot behind the site's forms uses up only its own network's allowance. This budget is separate from sign-ins. A 503 when the token could not be checked (Cloudflare cannot be reached).
Sign this device out. Its token stops working.

get.summary: The signed-in customer's account, with their unread notification count.

patch.summary: Change the customer's names. Only the names sent change; the answer is the same as `GET /me`. A 422 on the field: a blank first name, a name over 64 characters, or any name on an account with Telegram (its names come from Telegram).

post.summary: Prove a way into this account again. Changing how the account signs in needs a sign-in from the last 15 minutes; an older session gets a 403 and calls this first. Prove the account's password (with the authenticator app's code or a recovery code while two-factor sign-in is on), its Telegram account (the popup's id_token with a nonce from `POST /auth/nonce`, or the redirect's code with the state from `POST /me/telegram/authorize` for this session and the verifier of its challenge), or its Google account. The session may then change the account's ways in for 15 minutes. A 422 on `method` for anything but password, telegram or google; a 422 (no field) while the website has that sign-in method off; a 422 on `password` for an account without a password (prove another way); a 422 on the field when it is missing, the proof does not hold (`password`, `code` or `id_token`) or it proves another account. A 429 after too many failures (counted like sign-ins; a code also counts against the account's second-step budget); a 502 when the provider cannot be reached.

200.description: Proven; the session counts as recently signed in

post.summary: Start a Telegram redirect for the signed-in customer. Used to add their Telegram account (`POST /me/identities/telegram`) or prove it again (`POST /me/reauthenticate`). Returns the address to send the browser to. The site makes the PKCE verifier, keeps it and sends only its challenge. The state belongs to this session alone: a sign-in, another customer or another device of theirs cannot use it, and nothing can without the verifier. A 422 while the website has no client secret, or on `redirect_uri` or `code_challenge`; a 429 once this address network asked for 120 nonces, states and codes in 10 minutes; a 503 while the shop holds its maximum of open sign-ins.

put.summary: Set or change the customer's password. The password signs in with their email. Every other session ends, this one stays, and the customer is notified. A 403 when the session's sign-in is not recent (call `POST /me/reauthenticate` first); a 422 when the account has no email, the current password (if the account has one) is missing or wrong (a wrong one counts as a failed sign-in), or the new one breaks the password rule; a 429 after too many failures.

get.summary: The devices the customer is signed in on, newest first. This one is marked `current`.

delete.summary: End one of the customer's sessions, this one included. Another customer's session is a 404.

post.summary: Start setting up two-factor sign-in. Returns a new secret for the customer's authenticator app (RFC 6238). It waits 15 minutes for the app's first code (`POST /me/2fa/enable`) and replaces any earlier one. A 403 when the session's sign-in is not recent; a 422 when the account has no email and password, or two-factor sign-in is already on.

200.description: The secret, and the otpauth address the app can scan

post.summary: Turn two-factor sign-in on. Send the app's first code for the secret from `POST /me/2fa/setup` (five tries). Returns ten recovery codes, shown only this once; the customer is notified. A 403 when the session's sign-in is not recent; a 422 when the account has no email and password, two-factor sign-in is already on, or on `code` when it is wrong or no secret is waiting (start the setup again).

200.description: On; the recovery codes, shown only this once

post.summary: Turn two-factor sign-in off. Needs the account's password; the customer is notified. A 403 when the session's sign-in is not recent; a 422 when it is not on, or on `password` when it is missing or wrong (a wrong one counts as a failed sign-in); a 429 after too many failures.

Add a Telegram account to the customer's account. Prove it as a Telegram sign-in does: the popup's id_token with its nonce, or the redirect's code with the state from `POST /me/telegram/authorize` for this customer and the verifier of its challenge (a sign-in's state or another customer's proves nothing here). If the Telegram account is already this account's or nobody's, the answer is the account (a new link takes its handle and names from Telegram, and the customer is notified). If another account of the shop has it, a merge is offered (202). A 403 when the session's sign-in is not recent; a 422 when the proof does not hold (on `id_token` or the redirect's `code`), the account already has another Telegram account, the merge is not allowed, or Telegram sign-in is off; a 429 after too many failures; a 502 when Telegram cannot be reached.

200.description: The account, with the Telegram account linked

202.description: Another account has it; a merge is offered

post.summary: Add a Google account to the customer's account. Send the id_token Google Identity Services gave the page, with its nonce. If the Google account is already this account's or nobody's, the answer is the account; a new link also takes the email address Google vouches for (an @gmail.com or Workspace address) when the account has no email and no other account has it, and the customer is notified. If another account of the shop has the Google account or that address, a merge is offered (202). A 403 when the session's sign-in is not recent; a 422 when the proof does not hold (on `id_token`), the account already has another Google account, the merge is not allowed, or Google sign-in is off; a 429 after too many failures; a 502 when Google cannot be reached.

200.description: The account, with the Google account linked

post.summary: Add an email and password to the customer's account. Emails a six-digit code to the address (finish with `POST /me/identities/email/verify`), whether or not another account has the address: it is proven first. Another customer's pending code for the same address is not affected. A 403 when the session's sign-in is not recent; a 422 when the account already has an email or a field is invalid. A 429 when a code went to the address in the last minute, the address got its 10 emails today (counted across all shops), this address network sent its 20 an hour or asked too often, the address is locked after failed codes (10 wrong an hour, 20 a day), or this account asked for 5 codes today. A 502 when the email could not be sent; a 503 when the shop sends no email or its email budget is spent.

Finish adding an email with the emailed code. Only the account the code was sent for can use it. The address and its password become this account's and the customer is notified. If another account of the shop has the address, a merge is offered (202); after the merge, the remaining account has the address and the chosen password. A 403 when the session's sign-in is not recent; a 422 when the account already has an email, the merge is not allowed, or on `code` when it is wrong, expired, used, tried five times or another account's; a 429 after too many failures, or when the budget of wrong codes for the address or this account is spent (10 an hour, 20 a day).

202.description: Another account has it; a merge is offered

get.summary: What the shop sells now, as the bot's «خرید اشتراک» offers it. Every active category in order (empty ones too), then the plans with no category (or a switched-off one) as a group without a category. A plan is listed only while it can be delivered: switched on, on a server that can sell it, and in an agent's shop covered by the agent's traffic. Each plan lists the servers a customer can pick. Anyone may read it. With a customer's bearer token it is priced for that customer: `first_purchase_price` is null once they have bought, and `agent_price` is set only for an agent or a member of a group with agent prices. A token that is not valid is a 401, never the guest catalogue.

One plan, as `GET /plans` shows it. For a guest, or priced for the customer whose bearer token is sent. A 404 for a plan not on sale now: switched off, on no server able to deliver it, or (in an agent's shop) more than the agent's traffic covers.
Server status. The servers of the plans on sale, in order: whether each takes new customers now and when the shop last reached it. Never their addresses, connectors or panel messages.

«سرویس دلخواه»: what a customer may build — a service of the traffic and days they choose, on one of the builder's servers, with the builder's devices. Each quantity has its tiers (the whole quantity priced at the rate of the tier it falls into; the GB's price and the days' price added), its bounds and the amounts offered as buttons; any whole amount within the bounds may be chosen. `offered` says whether one may be built now: the main shop's alone, while its admin switches it on (off by default), both price lists sell and one of its servers can take a new client (`servers`, empty otherwise — and no tiers or buttons then). Anyone may read it; the customer's own price is `POST /custom-services/quote`.

post.summary: What a service the customer builds would cost them, nothing ordered: the GB's price and the days' price by their tiers, their sum (`base`), the customer's automatic discount and — with `discount_code` — the code's, as lines, and what is left. Only a sale of every plan reaches a built service, and a code limited to certain plans never does; a code limited to certain servers holds once `server_id` is picked. A 422 on `status` while nothing may be built (`offered` of `GET /custom-services`); on `gb` or `days` for an amount that is no whole number or outside its bounds (the message says them); on `server_id` for a server not on offer now; on `discount_code` when it does not apply. Each code that does not apply uses one of the customer's 20 tries an hour (shared with the checkout's), then a 429 with `Retry-After`.

Buy a service the customer builds, paid with `method_id`: the same checkout as `POST /orders`, as the bot's «🛠 ساخت سرویس دلخواه» buys it, at `POST /custom-services/quote`'s price. The order is a purchase without a plan (`plan` null) carrying its own `traffic_bytes`, `days` and `devices`; once delivered, its service has no plan either. `server_id` may be left out while the builder sells on one server. The service is named as `POST /orders` names one (`name_mode`, `client_name`). A 422 on `status` while nothing may be built; on `gb` or `days` for an amount that is no whole number or outside its bounds; on `server_id` for none picked among several servers, or a server not on offer now; on `name_mode` or `client_name` as `POST /orders` refuses them; on `method_id` for a method that cannot pay it, or a wallet short of the price; on `discount_code` when it does not apply; on `idempotency_key` for a key used for a different order or first sent with another `method_id`. The 5 unpaid orders, a receipt still in review, the 409s, the 429 past 30 ordering requests in 10 minutes and the 503 while the bot is switched off are `POST /orders`' own. Repeated with the same `Idempotency-Key`, it returns the order that key made, as it is now: never a second order or a second charge.

get.summary: The approved reviews, newest first, a page at a time. `meta.summary` covers all of them: their count and average rating. A 404 while the website shows no reviews (`reviews_enabled`, off by default).

post.summary: Write a review. Send the signed name, 1 to 5 stars, the text, an optional line on where the service is used, and an optional avatar from the website's own set. It waits for support to approve it (then `GET /reviews` shows it) or reject it; the report group is notified. Guests may write while the website asks for a captcha; without one, a guest gets a 403 (sign in first). With a bearer token the review is that customer's; a token that is not valid is a 401 (never a guest review instead), and a banned customer gets a 403. A 404 while the website takes no reviews (`reviews_enabled`, off by default). A 422 lists every invalid field at once: `name` (2 to 64 characters), `rating` (1 to 5), `body` (10 to 600), `context` (at most 100) or `avatar` (1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9, - and _: a key, never an address); then `captcha` while the website asks for one. A 429 with `Retry-After` past 20 reviews an hour from one address network (IPv6 counted by /48; refused captchas included), 3 a day from one customer, or 20 an hour from all guests together (refused captchas not included). A 503 while 200 reviews wait for support (no new review is accepted until support decides some), or when the captcha could not be checked.

get.summary: The customer's services, newest first. In one status, or all.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only services with this status. None for all

post.summary: Add a service to the customer's account by its link («افزودن سرویس با لینک»), as the bot does. `link` is the text the customer sent: a subscription link or one of the service's configs (vless://, vmess://, trojan://, ss://, hysteria2://, tuic://), alone or among other words; its links are read together, five at most. The shop asks its panels whose client it is and adds it as its panel has it, with no plan (`plan` null, `claimed_at` set) until its first renewal (`GET …/renewal-plans`); the report group is told. The first customer to send it gets it. Only while the shop offers it (`shop.service_claims` of `GET /`): the main shop's alone, off by default. Refusals are on `link`: a 422 while it is off, for text with no link in it (or longer than 2000 characters), for a link no panel has, for a service already the customer's own, or one whose panel serves it no subscription link; a 409 for a service already in another customer's account; a 502 when a panel that might have it did not answer. Each link sent asks every panel: at most 10 links in 10 minutes per customer, then a 429 with `Retry-After`.

201.description: Added: the service, as `GET /subscriptions/{id}` shows it

get.summary: One of the customer's services, as last read from its panel (`synced_at`). Another customer's service is a 404.

patch.summary: Switch the service's auto-renewal («تمدید خودکار») on or off. When on, the service is renewed from the wallet before it ends. A 422 on `auto_renew` while auto-renewal is not offered (`auto_renew.offered`), or for anything but a boolean.

post.summary: Read the service from its panel now, with whether it is connected (`presence`). A client the panel no longer has comes back as deleted. A 502 when the panel cannot be read now (unreachable, or skipped for a while after a failure); the shop's stored copy is not returned instead. At most 10 reads a minute per customer, then a 429 with `Retry-After`.

Change the service's subscription link (`link_rotation`). Every device on the old link is disconnected; the bot sends no message about it. A 422 on `status` when the service is not active or its server cannot rotate links; a 409 while another change to it is running; a 502 when the server failed. At most 5 an hour per customer, then a 429 with `Retry-After`.

200.description: The service, with its new link

get.summary: «انتقال سرویس», before it is done: who the shop's customer with this numeric Telegram id is (their Telegram name and handle), so the website asks the customer to confirm them before `POST`. The same refusals as `POST`, nothing changed. Each look-up counts: at most 10 in 10 minutes per customer, together with `GET /wallet/transfer`, then a 429 with `Retry-After`.

parameters.name: telegram_id
parameters.description: The recipient's numeric Telegram id (Persian digits are read too).

post.summary: «انتقال سرویس»: hand the service to another customer of the shop, found by their numeric Telegram id, for free — as the bot does it. Only while the shop lets customers (`shop.service_transfers` of `GET /`, off by default). The service keeps its link, term and traffic and is the recipient's from now on (this customer's `GET /subscriptions/{id}` is a 404 after it); its «تمدید خودکار» goes off; the link goes with it, so this customer's devices stay connected until the recipient changes it (`POST /subscriptions/{id}/rotate-link`); the recipient is told in the bot and among their notices (`service_received`, which says so where the link can change) — this customer is not: the answer is theirs; the report group hears of it. A 403 when the session's sign-in is not recent (call `POST /me/reauthenticate` first): a bearer token alone gives no service away. A 422 on `status` while the shop does not offer it, for a free test account, a service gone from its panel or being changed on it right then (try again in a moment), or one with an order this customer made not finished with (a renewal or an extra awaiting its payment or receipt, or being delivered; an unpaid one is dropped by itself after 48 hours, unless its card transfer went to support's private chat, which support approves or cancels; one whose delivery failed waits for support, and its message says to ask them); on `telegram_id` for an id that is no number, that names no customer of this shop (they must have started the bot once), the customer themselves, or a banned account. It looks the recipient up as `GET` does (one of its 10 in 10 minutes); at most 5 services handed on an hour per customer, then a 429 with `Retry-After`.

get.summary: Preview a service's renewal. As the bot's «♻️ تمدید سرویس» shows it: on the service's own plan, at that plan's price today, and the service as the renewal would leave it (its term, its traffic, and the unused traffic of the current period that expires when the period ends). A service without a plan (added by its link, `claimed_at`, or built) is renewed on a plan the customer picks, `plan_id`, among `GET …/renewal-plans`: a 422 on `plan_id` when none is picked, or one that is not among them. While the shop's builder is offered for it (`custom_services` of `GET …/renewal-plans`), it may be renewed instead with a package the customer builds, `gb` and `days` (as `POST /custom-services/quote` takes them; the answer's `custom`), which leaves it without a plan: a 422 on `status` while the builder is not offered, on `gb` or `days` as the builder refuses them or for a service renewed on its own plan, on `plan_id` sent with them. A 422 on `status` while it cannot be renewed (switched off by support, gone from its panel, a free test account, its plan renewing nothing, without a plan while neither a plan on sale is sold on its server nor the builder is offered, or in an agent's shop more than the agent's traffic covers), or while a renewal of it is in progress (its receipt is with support, or it is paid and being delivered). A 422 on `status` too while the shop does not let it be renewed yet (`renewal_window`), saying from when: «تمدید این سرویس از … ممکن است.»; and while — an agent's shop — the main shop suspended its selling, in the words the `POST` then answers with a 503 («فروش این فروشگاه فعلا متوقف است؛ …»). By the renewal method `method`, one of the shop's (`methods` in the answer; the first when left out): a 422 on `method` for one it does not offer.

parameters.name: plan_id
parameters.description: For a service without a plan (`picks_plan`): the plan to renew it on, one of `GET …/renewal-plans`. For a service with its own plan it may be left out; sent, it must be that plan (a 422 on `plan_id` otherwise: the service got a plan since the page was drawn).

parameters.name: gb
parameters.description: For a service without a plan, instead of `plan_id` while the builder is offered for it: the GB of a package the customer builds, within the bounds of `GET /custom-services`. With `days`.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: With `gb`: the days of that package, within the bounds of `GET /custom-services`.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: The renewal method to preview by, one of the shop's (`methods`); left out, the first of them.

post.summary: Renew a service, paid with `method_id`, as the GET previews it: by the renewal method `method`, and a service without a plan on the plan `plan_id` picks, which becomes its plan once the renewal is delivered — or with the package `gb` and `days` build, an order without a plan carrying its own `traffic_bytes`, `days` and `devices`, after which the service still has none (so «تمدید خودکار» never renews it). The wallet renews it at once; a card waits for its receipt (`POST /payments/{id}/receipt`). Refused for the same reasons as the GET, and as `POST /orders` (a 422 on `method_id` when the wallet is short; a 422 with too many unpaid orders, or on `status` with a receipt still in review; a 409 when the order was paid or closed at the same moment elsewhere; a 429 past the checkout's rate limit; a 503 while the shop takes no orders — its bot switched off, or its selling suspended, which the GET answers with a 422 on `status`). Repeated with the same `Idempotency-Key` (and the same `plan_id`, or `gb` and `days`, and `method`), it returns the renewal that key made, as it is now.

get.summary: The plans a service can be renewed on now, each at the customer's renewal price today. For a service without a plan (added by its link, `claimed_at`, or built) that is no test account: the plans on sale that are sold on its server and give a renewal something, in the catalogue's order, for the customer to pick one (`plan_id` of `…/renewal`); the renewal makes it the service's plan. For any other service: its own plan. Empty — and `custom_services` false — while the service cannot be renewed now: not at all, not yet (its `renewal_window` closed), or a renewal of it under way (as `…/renewal` would refuse it). `custom_services` says whether a service without a plan may be renewed with a package the customer builds instead (`gb` and `days` of `…/renewal`).

The extra traffic, time and devices a service can buy now. As the bot's «🔋 حجم اضافه», «⏳ زمان اضافه» and «👥 کاربر اضافه» offer them, at the plan's own prices or else the shop's: each kind's preset amounts with their prices and, when there is a price per GB, day or device, any amount within `custom`. Devices are priced for 30 days and charged for the days left of the period in use (`days`), which they last; their prices here are already that share. A kind is null when none can be bought: the shop does not sell it, or the service cannot take it. (`StoreSubscription.extras` gives the same answer as one flag per kind; a refused POST explains why.)

post.summary: Buy extra traffic for a service. `gb` paid with `method_id`, through the same checkout as every purchase. The wallet adds it at once (a service whose traffic ran out runs again); a card waits for its receipt (`POST /payments/{id}/receipt`). A 422 on `status` while the service cannot take it (switched off by support, gone from its panel, a free test account, unlimited, or its time ran out); on `gb` for an amount not on offer, or when none is sold (see `GET …/extras`); on `method_id` and `idempotency_key` as for `POST /orders`. The 422s for five unpaid orders and a receipt still in review, and the 409, 429 and 503, as for `POST /orders`. Repeated with the same `Idempotency-Key`, it returns the order that key made, as it is now.

Buy extra time for a service. `days` paid with `method_id`, through the same checkout as every purchase. The wallet adds it at once: onto the service's end, or, if its time ran out, as a new term starting at its next connection. A card waits for its receipt. A 422 on `status` while the service cannot take it (switched off by support, gone from its panel, a free test account, never expiring, or its traffic ran out); on `days` for an amount not on offer, or when none is sold (see `GET …/extras`); on `method_id` and `idempotency_key` as for `POST /orders`. The 422s for five unpaid orders and a receipt still in review, and the 409, 429 and 503, as for `POST /orders`. Repeated with the same `Idempotency-Key`, it returns the order that key made, as it is now.

Buy extra devices for a service («کاربر اضافه»): `devices` more on its IP limit, paid with `method_id`, through the same checkout as every purchase. Priced for 30 days and charged for the days left of the period in use (whole days, at least 1: to its end date, or to the start of a renewal bought before then; its whole term while it waits for its first connection; 30 for one that never ends), rounded up to whole Toman — as `GET …/extras` shows. The devices last until that period ends: a renewal brings its own device limit (`StoreRenewal`), and they are bought again for the new period. The wallet adds them at once; a card waits for its receipt. A 422 on `status` while the service cannot take them (switched off by support, gone from its panel, a free test account, an unlimited device limit, its time or traffic ran out, or a server whose panel does not enforce the limit); on `devices` for an amount not on offer, or when none is sold (see `GET …/extras`); on `method_id` and `idempotency_key` as for `POST /orders`. The 422s for five unpaid orders and a receipt still in review, and the 409, 429 and 503, as for `POST /orders`. Repeated with the same `Idempotency-Key`, it returns the order that key made, as it is now.

get.summary: The payment methods for a kind of order, in checkout order. The same as the bot's checkout offers: every enabled method, except the wallet for a wallet top-up — and, given the amount to pay, only the methods that take it: within their bounds (`min_amount`, `max_amount`), and a card-to-card method with a card that has room for it today — or one the customer holds an unpaid payment of, for that kind and amount, which asking again shows them on its card.

parameters.name: amount

post.summary: Buy a plan on one of its locations, paid with `method_id`. The same checkout as the bot's purchases, at the customer's price: the lowest of the price, the first-purchase price (`first_purchase_price`, until they have bought a service) and the agent price (`agent_price`, for an agent or a member of a group with agent prices). The order is created only with the payment method. The service is named on its panel by the shop's pattern, or — while the shop offers it (`shop.name_modes` of `GET /`) — by a random name or the one the customer typed (`name_mode`, `client_name`). The wallet pays at once (the service is delivered, or the order fails and waits for support); a card waits for its receipt (`POST /payments/{id}/receipt`). A 422 on `plan_id` for a plan not on sale now (switched off, on no location that can deliver it now, or in an agent's shop more traffic than the agent has left to sell); on `server_id` for a server it is not sold on now while another location is; on `name_mode` for a way of naming the shop does not offer; on `client_name` for a typed name that is refused; on `method_id` for a method that cannot pay it, or a wallet short of the price (the message says how much is missing); on `idempotency_key` for a key used for a different order or first sent with another `method_id`. A 422 (no field) while the customer has 5 unpaid orders; paid or expired orders free the room. A 422 on `status` for a card method while the shop takes one receipt at a time and the customer's last receipt is still in review (the message names its order; nothing is ordered, and the wallet still pays). A 409 when the order was paid or closed at the same moment elsewhere, or, for a repeated request, when the order was cancelled since (with its own message). A 429 with `Retry-After` past 30 ordering requests in 10 minutes (purchases, renewals and top-ups together, repeats included). A 503 while the shop takes no orders because its bot is switched off or — an agent's shop — the main shop suspended its selling (`shop.taking_orders` of `GET /`), repeats included. Repeated with the same `Idempotency-Key`, it returns the order that key made, as it is now: never a second order or a second charge.

get.summary: One of the customer's orders, with its payments. Another customer's order is a 404.

post.summary: Upload the receipt of a card transfer. For the payment the checkout returned (`transfer.payment_id`): a picture, with an optional note from the customer. Support always reviews it (in the panel or the report group): a card method's automatic approval window applies only to receipts sent in the bot, never to uploads. Returns the order, with the payment awaiting review. A 404 for another customer's payment; a 422 on `status` while the payment awaits no receipt (one was already sent, or it was rejected, paid, cancelled, or is not a card transfer), or while the shop takes one receipt at a time and another receipt of the customer's is still in review (the message names its order), on `file` when it is not a JPEG, PNG or WebP of at most 10 MB, or on `note` when it is too long. A 429 with `Retry-After` past 10 pictures in an hour (receipts and ticket pictures share this budget). A 503 while the host has less than 200 MB of free disk, once the shop's uploads for the day reach 1024 MB, or while the shop takes no orders (its bot is switched off). A form larger than PHP accepts is a 413; a form field that is not UTF-8 is a 422 on that field.

post.summary: Top up the wallet by `amount`, paid with `method_id`. The amount must be within the `top_up` limits of `GET /wallet` (else a 422 on `amount` stating them). Any method but the wallet itself (else a 422 on `method_id`). A card waits for its receipt (`POST /payments/{id}/receipt`); once paid, the amount is added to the balance. Refused like `POST /orders` for too many unpaid orders or a receipt still in review (422), past the checkout's rate limit (429) and while the shop takes no orders (503). Repeated with the same `Idempotency-Key`, it returns the top-up that key made, as it is now.

The same refusals as `POST` about the recipient, nothing changed: a 422 on `status` while the shop offers none (`transfer` of `GET /wallet` is null); on `amount` while the customer can send nothing now — less than `min` in the wallet, or the daily cap used up (its `most` below `min`) —, before any id is looked up; on `telegram_id` for an id that is no number, that names no customer of this shop (they must have started the bot once), the customer themselves, or a banned account. Each look-up counts: at most 10 in 10 minutes per customer, together with `GET /subscriptions/{id}/transfer`, then a 429 with `Retry-After`.

post.summary: «انتقال موجودی»: send `amount` from the wallet to another customer of the shop, found by their numeric Telegram id — as the bot does it, with no fee. Only while the shop offers it (`transfer` of `GET /wallet`, off by default), and only from the wallet's own balance, never an agent's credit. The recipient's wallet gets the whole amount at once; each wallet's ledger has a line naming the other customer («انتقال موجودی به …», «دریافت موجودی از …»); the recipient is told in the bot and among their notices (`wallet_received`), this customer among their notices and in Telegram (`wallet_sent`); the report group hears of it. A 403 when the session's sign-in is not recent (call `POST /me/reauthenticate` first): a bearer token alone gives no money away. A 422 on `status` while the shop offers none; on `telegram_id` as `GET` refuses it; on `amount` for no whole number of Toman, below `min` or above `max`, more than the balance, or past the daily cap (the message says what today leaves); on `idempotency_key` for a missing or malformed key, or one sent before with another recipient or amount. It looks the recipient up as `GET` does (one of its 10 in 10 minutes); at most 10 transfers an hour per customer, then a 429 with `Retry-After`. Repeated with the same `Idempotency-Key`, it answers the transfer that key made, with the wallet as it is now: never a second transfer.

post.summary: Check a discount code before paying. Returns the quote the order would be made at: the base price (the customer's price for the plan, or the cost of that much extra), the automatic discount and the code's discount as lines, and the total. Nothing is ordered. A 422 on `code` when it does not apply: unknown in this shop, switched off, outside its dates, for another type of order, plan or server, only for a first purchase, for a larger order, or used up. The rest of the request is refused as its checkout would refuse it: a 422 on `plan_id`, `server_id`, `status`, `gb`, `days` or `devices`, a 404 for a service not theirs — in an agent's shop whose selling the main shop suspended, a purchase on `plan_id` and a renewal or an extra on `status`, where the checkout answers a 503. Each code that does not apply uses one of the customer's 20 tries an hour (shared with the checkout's `discount_code`), then a 429 with `Retry-After`.

Redeem a gift code, as the bot's «🎁 کد هدیه» does. The code may be typed in any case, with dashes and spaces anywhere and Persian digits. Toman are added to the wallet; a plan code delivers a free service (the answer has its order and, once delivered, the service; nothing is sent in Telegram). A 422 on `code` when the shop takes no codes now, the code does not exist, is already redeemed (by them or someone else) or expired, or its service cannot be delivered now (the code stays theirs to try again). Every try that names no code of the shop counts against the customer and their address network: 10 wrong tries an hour per customer and 30 per network, then a 429 with `Retry-After`.

post.description:
Support makes a new service for the customer: a plan (`plan_id`) on one of its servers that can deliver it now, or
a service of its own numbers (`traffic_gb`, `days`, `devices`; 0 for no limit) on any server that can take one now
(`server_id`). It is named `client_name` when given (held to the rules a buyer's own name is: 3 to 32 Latin
letters, digits, `_` and `-`, taken by the server's panel, free there), else by the shop's pattern. `payment` says
how it is paid: `free` (a gift), `wallet` (`amount` charged to the customer's wallet, while the shop's wallet is
switched on) or `outside` (`amount` support took outside the shop, cash or another card — counted in the
shop's takings). The order is delivered at once, in an agent's shop out of the agent's traffic; the customer is
told once it is, and the report group's «خریدها» says support made it. A delivery that fails leaves the order
`failed` for a retry (`POST /orders/{id}/retry`), which tells the customer.

How each counts: a free order is a gift — no purchase of the customer's (a first-purchase price and a newcomer's
code stay theirs), no takings, no referrer's commission or gift, no cashback, nothing towards loyalty tiers or the
draw. A wallet order is a purchase at that amount (cashback, loyalty and a referral's first-purchase gift count it)
but no takings and no commission: the wallet's money counted when it came in. An outside order is the same
purchase and the shop's takings too, earning the referrer's commission.

A 403 for an admin's own account on the website's admin API. A 422 under the field refused: `status` (an agent's
shop whose selling is suspended: none is made there, by the owner neither, until it sells again), `payment`
(`wallet` while the shop's wallet is switched off), `amount` (not a whole number above zero, or more than the wallet

Refund a paid payment. For a purchase, a renewal or an agent's traffic, the amount goes to the customer's wallet; a wallet top-up is taken back out of the wallet. A 422 on `note` over 190 characters (it becomes the wallet line's description) or on `status`, and also when what the order added is gone or cannot be taken back (a top-up already spent, an agent's traffic already sold, a service whose panel fails, a purchase's service another paid or open order holds, a service handed to another customer since): then nothing is refunded. customer.description: A website customer's session: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, with the token from their sign-in (64 hex characters), one per device. Once the session ends, every request with its token is a 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`, and the customer signs in again. A session ends when the customer signs that device out (`POST /auth/logout`) or ends it from another device (`DELETE /me/sessions/{id}`); when their password is changed (`PUT /me/password`, or set by a merge: every session except the one that changed it) or reset (`POST /auth/password/reset` or its second step: every session); when support signs them out of every device from a panel; when a 21st session opens (the oldest ends: at most 20 per customer); after 30 days unused; and 180 days after the sign-in. A banned customer's token gets a 403. Changing how the account signs in, and handing a service to another customer (`POST /subscriptions/{id}/transfer`), also need a recent sign-in: within 15 minutes, or a way in proven again since (`POST /me/reauthenticate`). Otherwise the answer is a 403 whose `WWW-Authenticate` says so (`Bearer error="insufficient_user_authentication", max_age=900`).

Panel.name: panel
Panel.description: Which panel: the owner's (`admin`) or an agent's (`agent`). The operation is the same screen in both

Shop.name: X-Shop
Shop.description: The shop the request works in, by its bot's id (`ShopRef.id`; 1 is the main bot). The owner's panel sends the shop its tab shows, taken from the tab's address (`/admin/s/7/…`; `/admin/…` is the main bot), so the session remembers no shop and two tabs can work in two shops. Without it, the request works in the main shop. A value that is not a bot id is a 422 on `shop`; a bot that does not exist is a 404 on `shop` (never the main shop instead), for a sign-in too once its credentials are right. A sign-in returns the session in the shop named. Sections that cover the whole installation ignore it: servers work across every bot's services, and the agency and the panel settings always work in the main shop. An agent's panel sends none, since their shop is their bot; naming another bot is a 403 on `shop`.

ShopQuery.name: shop
